small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_SP configs (512) and try BLOCK_OC tile smaller than OC (e.g., 32) with an OC-loop reduction so register pressure drops and BLOCK_SP can grow; current BLOCK_OC=64 with BLOCK_SP=256 uses a 64×256 acc tile in registers.
- Sweep num_warps={8,16} and num_stages={2,3,4} at BLOCK_SP=256/512 — the kernel is compute/MMA heavy and may benefit from more pipelining of the KH*KW loop's loads.
- Try a channels-last input layout (NHWC) so the IC dimension is contiguous and the [IC, BLOCK_SP] gather becomes a contiguous load along K — this should significantly improve memory throughput on the inner dot.
large_guidance:
- Restructure to one program per (N, output-spatial-tile) producing only the min directly: keep accumulator as [BLOCK_OC_TILE, BLOCK_SP] but loop over OC in tiles, maintaining a running min vector of shape [BLOCK_SP] so register footprint is small and BLOCK_SP can be 512+.
- Switch to NHWC input layout and pack weight as [KH*KW, IC, OC] (or [KH*KW*IC, OC]) so the inner GEMM is (BLOCK_SP, IC) × (IC, BLOCK_OC) with all contiguous loads; this matches Triton's MMA layout better than the current [OC,IC]×[IC,SP].
- Consider a persistent-CTA design with a 2D spatial tile (e.g., 16×16) instead of flattened 1D so adjacent KH/KW offsets reuse cached input rows, improving L1 reuse for the 3×3 stencil.
